subject: Cobalt Ridge: SLA remediation & credit routing after 2027-03-14 deploy impact
messages:
From: Tess Warner <tess.warner@cobaltridge.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Idris Patel <idris.patel@cobaltridge.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Degraded throughput after Friday deploy — impact to SLA

Hi Priyom,

We saw a significant drop in inference throughput and a spike in 5xx errors between 02:30-04:10 UTC on 2027-03-14 following your scheduled model deploy. This materially affected our production feature (recommendation API) and caused increased fallbacks. Our platform team ran initial diagnostics and collected logs — attaching a short snippet.

Can you confirm whether this window qualifies for SLA remediation? We need an estimate of eligible credit and timeline for issuance so we can reconcile vendor billing for Q1.

Thanks,
Tess
Tess Warner
Director, Platform Engineering
Cobalt Ridge Systems

Attachment: support_log_snippet.txt (text, 18KB)

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Tess Warner <tess.warner@cobaltridge.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Degraded throughput after Friday deploy — impact to SLA

Tess — thanks for the report and logs. We investigated: a model variant fallback combined with an autoscaler constraint caused queueing and higher 5xx during that window. We've pulled the raw serving metrics and attached a condensed uptime report and an SLO worksheet with the preliminary calc.

Short answers:
- Eligibility: likely eligible for service credit under section 4.2 of our SLA (availability for dedicated customers).
- Preliminary credit estimate: ~6.1% of monthly committed spend for March (see workbook).
- Next steps: internal approval for issuance (finance + legal), then we provide a credit note and DocuSign for the adjustment.

I'll loop in Lauren and Ben to get the calc validated and to coordinate approval. Appreciate the logs — they helped isolate the time slices.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: uptime_report_20270315.csv; slo_calc_workbook.xlsx

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Degraded throughput after Friday deploy — impact to SLA

Folks — I validated the calc in the workbook. Key points:
- Total incident window considered: 02:28–04:12 UTC (104 minutes).
- Effective downtime (unavailable per SLA definition): 48 minutes (periods where successful request rate < 95% of baseline).
- Monthly committed uptime basis: 43,200 minutes (30-day month).
- Credit fraction = downtime / month = 48/43200 = 0.111% → rounding conventions in our SLA yield 0.11% credit.
- However, the customer is on a committed spend tier with a minimum remedial slab (we cap micro-credits at $50). Given their monthly commit, 0.11% maps to ~6.1% of their monthly invoice based on token-based billing reconciliation in the workbook (explain: credit formula combines % downtime with token-weighted usage during incident).

I left comments in the sheet about the token-weighted adjustment and a suggested wording for the credit note. If legal wants to sign off, we can generate the DocuSign package.

—Lauren
Sr. Revenue Ops Analyst, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 10:41:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Degraded throughput after Friday deploy — impact to SLA

Hi team — ran the numbers against billing records and HubSpot usage snapshot. Confirming:
- Final credit amount: $12,420.00 (net of prepaid credits & prorations).
- Reason: eligible downtime + token-weighted usage multiplier for recommendation model.
- Proposed issuance path: internal credit memo -> DocuSign acknowledgment (customer) -> accounting posts AR adjustment next cycle.

Kimberly, can you confirm expedited approval path? This customer flagged a Q1 reconciliation deadline (end of March). If we can approve before 24 Mar, they can close their books cleanly.

Thanks,
Ben
Revenue Operations

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Degraded throughput after Friday deploy — impact to SLA

Thanks team. Approving the credit of $12,420. Priyom — please prepare the credit memo and the DocuSign packet. Include the incident summary language in the memo (root cause: model-variant fallback + autoscaler constraint; mitigation: adjusted autoscaler thresholds and canary rollback workflow added).

I'll route to Finance for booking; Lauren, please attach the calc and place the final value in the accounting template. We will aim to have the DocuSign out by 2027-03-18.

Kimberly Park
Head of Revenue Operations

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Tess Warner <tess.warner@cobaltridge.com>
Cc: Idris Patel <idris.patel@cobaltridge.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 16:23:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Degraded throughput after Friday deploy — impact to SLA

Tess — thanks for your patience. Internal approvals are complete and we've authorized a service credit of $12,420 to Cobalt Ridge Systems for the March billing period.

What's next:
1) You'll receive a DocuSign packet (CBR-8421) to acknowledge the credit note and adjusted invoice. Link will arrive from DocuSign shortly.
2) Accounting will post the credit in the next AR run after we receive the signed acknowledgment.
3) Technical follow-up: our infra team deployed autoscaler threshold fixes and added a canary rollback gate to prevent recurrence. We'll share the postmortem doc by EOD Friday.

Attached are the supporting files (uptime report and calc workbook). Please let me know if you need the credit split across projects or a different billing handle.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Account Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: uptime_report_20270315.csv; slo_calc_workbook.xlsx
DocuSign link: https://docusign.example/sign/CBR-8421
